clue.text: Type of garden that's a right pain in the neck — and stomach

parts.note: taken as written
a tiresome person or thing is a bore
tum is a colloquial word for the stomach

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a certain garden gives them aches in the neck and the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical collection planted with trees, a specialised kind of garden.

clue.text: Bitter and cold, but dry outside

indicators.note: the word for dry sits outside, wrapping round the letter for cold

parts.note: arid means dry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A description of weather, or a drink, that is sharp, chilly and parched.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and harsh to taste or smell, a synonym of bitter.

clue.text: Black and white mostly suffering for popular movement

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is used, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: agony means intense suffering

explanation.surface: Something monochrome and nearly in pain is offered up as a fashionable trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from AGONY to leave AGON.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump on the bandwagon is to join a fashionable cause, so the word names a popular movement.

clue.text: Tear outside in response to withdrawal

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the word for response

parts.note: a reaction is a response

indicators.note: outside asks for the outer letters of the word Tear, its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone sheds a tear outdoors when their offer is pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' looks like crying or ripping; only its first and last letters are used, which 'outside' signals, and 'in' places them within the word for response.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction is the taking back of a statement, a withdrawal of it.

clue.text: Air passage when the car needs a service

indicators.note: a service takes a car apart and puts it right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motoring remark about when a vehicle is due for its garage check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' rearranges THE CAR into TRACHE, and A is added at the end; 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the tube carrying breath to the lungs.

clue.text: Handout?

parts.note: read as 'hand out', a hand of cards dealt out wrongly, rather than charity given away

explanation.surface: A one-word query about charity given to the needy.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdeal is a faulty distribution of cards, a hand dealt out in error.

clue.text: Human sponge drinking at home

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to sponge off someone is to cadge, or beg
in means at home

explanation.surface: A person who freeloads stays home with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is a living creature, as in a human being.

clue.text: One may be passed by this young man

definitions.text: One may be passed by this

explanation.definitionFit: Passing the buck shifts responsibility; a buck is also a dashing young fellow.

clue.text: Picture, for instance, holding review

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps the other within it

parts.note: i.e. (that is) stands in here for the phrase introducing an example
a review can be a periodical, a magazine, shortened to mag

explanation.surface: An example given of a picture that contains a critique.
explanation.walkthrough: I.E. strictly means 'that is', but the setter uses it for 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Soldier who collapsed near ridge

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier falls down close to a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is an infantryman, originally one who threw grenades.

clue.text: Game point with a team's first attack

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, a game
N is a compass point, north

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word team's

explanation.surface: In a match, a side scores with an early charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To run at someone is to charge at them, an attack.

clue.text: Link to a case is destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Evidence connecting someone to a crime has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate is to connect one thing with another, to link them.

clue.text: Shabby fur covering at bottom of leg

parts.note: down is the soft fine coat of hair or feathers covering a young animal
taken as written
the heel is at the bottom of the leg

explanation.surface: A worn-out fur coat reaches down to the ankles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone down at heel is scruffy and poor, like worn-down shoes.

clue.text: Girl whose age is beyond five

indicators.note: is beyond means placed after, so the word for age follows the numeral

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A girl who is older than five.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a girl's name.

clue.text: Time and motion studies come on rigs after reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Efficiency experts arrive at oil platforms after a management shake-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomics studies how people work efficiently with their equipment, close to time and motion study.

clue.text: Leaves after expensive meal

indicators.note: after places the word for leaves behind the word for expensive

parts.note: high prices are expensive ones
tea is made from leaves

explanation.surface: Someone departs after a costly dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb, departs; it is the noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is an early evening meal with tea, cooked food and cakes, a British tradition.

clue.text: Careless young lady, having first struck gold

indicators.note: having first means the other pieces go in front of the word for young lady

parts.note: struck means hit
or is gold in heraldry
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A slapdash young woman got lucky with a gold strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit-or-miss means haphazard, done without care or planning.

clue.text: An attractive nymph with the knowledge accumulated by Garland

indicators.note: accumulated by joins the word for knowledge to the garland that follows it

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: A captivating spirit gains wisdom through Judy Garland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a Rhine siren whose song lured boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: Built with care, in order to eliminate friction

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them anew

explanation.surface: Something constructed carefully so its parts run smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lubricate is to apply oil or grease so parts slide smoothly without rubbing.

clue.text: Wrapper that can frustrate?

parts.note: a tin is a can
to foil is to frustrate or thwart

explanation.surface: A wrapping that might thwart someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheet used to wrap food.

clue.text: Deposit found around stick vegetables

indicators.note: around means the word for deposit goes round the word for stick

parts.note: lees are the sediment deposited in wine
gum is an adhesive, used to stick things

explanation.surface: Some sediment is found around a stick of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes are pod-bearing plants such as peas, beans and lentils.

clue.text: Hit the right gear?

explanation.definitionFit: To clobber is to strike hard; clobber is also British slang for clothes and kit.

clue.text: Sign of error by editor that's passed over

parts.note: a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: An editor marks a mistake that was overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossed means gone across, passed over a road or river.

clue.text: Enveloped in sound, and held spellbound

indicators.note: in sound means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: enveloped means wrapped

explanation.surface: Someone wrapped in music listens in enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means wholly absorbed, as if under a spell.

clue.text: Quietly fascinated by horse

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone is silently entranced by a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse.

clue.text: Crop specialist who finds margins too awkward

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farming expert finds the edges of the field too hard to work.
explanation.definitionFit: An agronomist studies soil and crop production.

clue.text: Hair loss of leader from pressure

indicators.note: loss of leader means the first letter of the word for pressure is dropped

parts.note: stress means pressure

explanation.surface: Stress causes someone to start losing their hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock of hair.

clue.text: Worry about being so lost in forest

indicators.note: lost in means the given letters go missing from inside the word forest

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about getting lost in woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing SO from FOREST leaves FRET; 'about being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious.

clue.text: One who doesn't know how to aim guns or…

indicators.note: how to asks in what manner the letters may be put together, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ignorant person has no idea how to point weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the clue runs on into the next with its dots.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person.

clue.text: … very angry deserter that's found outside

indicators.note: outside means the abbreviation for that is goes round the word for deserter

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
a rat deserts, as from a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Furious about a runaway discovered out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means furious.

clue.text: Rugby chap who's a good egg…

explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is one kind of athletic game; a decent, fair-minded fellow is also called this.

clue.text: … avoids team dance

parts.note: a side is a team
steps are the movements of a dance

explanation.surface: A team dodges the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to evade or dodge.
